slides.text: Prime Agent Harness vs Hermes Prime Agent Harness vs Hermes Prime Intellect reports 95.5% on ARC-AGI-3 using Opus 5 (exceeding 95.4% human-expert baseline) Agent performance depends heavily on the scaffold (context management, tool design, memory, verification, and retry loops), not solely on model weights https://primeintellect.ai https://github.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent Prime Agent is an MIT-licensed, open-source agent harness Prime Agent wraps existing LLMs with a persistent Python environment, tools, and subagents Its recursive-language-model approach keeps large inputs external as variables The model writes code to inspect, filter, summarize, and delegate work instead of ingesting every token This targets “context rot,” where long inputs reduce accuracy before a model reaches its advertised context limit https://www.primeintellect.ai/blog/prime-agent https://www.primeintellect.ai/blog/recursive-language-models https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uY9tMU-KS4A Prime Agent vs Hermes Prime Agent excels at deep, long-running coding and research, using a persistent Python session and a private, editable learning harness; Lessons compound inside one agent. Hermes excels as a connected agent: tools, live search, MCP, multiple model providers, background workers, and shared external memory; A shared vault lets Hermes and other agents reuse business rules and history Choose Prime for focused autonomous work Choose Hermes for integrated workflows and team-wide context https://github.com/nousresearch/hermes-agent - 230K stars Long-context models suffer “context rot”: accuracy declines causing missed instructions, faulty retrieval, and confident errors, especially near a prompt’s center Recursive language models inspect stored document slices instead of loading everything into one prompt

slides.title: AI Updates Gauntlet Loop: AI QA Gauntlet Loop
slides.text: AI Updates Gauntlet Loop: AI QA Gauntlet Loop is an agentic workflow popularized by Matt Shumer : a lead agent decomposes a goal, then specialist builders and independent blind critics iteratively improve each inspectable component A gauntlet originally is a long protective glove, especially the armored glove worn by medieval knights. It later gained figurative meanings connected to challenge and hardship. “Run the gauntlet” means endure a difficult series of attacks, tests, or criticisms. So "Gauntlet Loop" means going through a multi-step challenges or criticism https://x.com/mattshumer_/status/2081830214384886228 https://x.com/mattshumer_/status/2081830741436928208 https://somethingbig.ai/gauntlet-loop https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XTONeqPuh_4 https://somethingbig.ai https://github.com/mshumer/Claude-of-Duty https://somethingbig.ai/gauntlet-loop The prompt for the Gauntlet Loop needs three essentials: .. an ambitious outcome, .. a concrete benchmark critics can inspect, .. an explicit stopping boundary Treat viral claims cautiously: blind evaluation, measurable tests, budget caps, and human acceptance remain essential; “utterly wowed” is not a reliable completion criterion Matt Shumer : AI entrepreneur and investor Co-founder of OthersideAI , the company behind the AI writing assistant HyperWrite He also invests in early-stage AI infrastructure and developer-tool companies through Shumer Capital He became widely visible for his February 2026 essay, “Something Big Is Happening,” which argued that the public is underestimating rapidly improving AI capabilities and their implications for knowledge work The post reportedly reached more than 80 million views and sparked substantial debate about whether its conclusions were too alarmist

slides.title: AI Updates Harness-R1: Outcome-Graded Agents 1. deploy AI
slides.text: AI Updates Harness-R1: Outcome-Graded Agents 1. deploy AI agent and collect every failure trajectory it produces 2. a separate 9B "harness engineer" reads those failures and diagnoses what keeps going wrong 3. the engineer writes executable code patches that change how the runtime feeds context, validates actions, and triggers recovery 4. the patched agent reruns the exact same tasks with its original weights frozen 5. only patches that actually raised task success survive and train the engineer further through reinforcement learning The harness can add start-of-task guidance, decision hints, pre-action guards, and post-feedback recovery instructions It raised the vanilla target’s average success from 44.3% to 53.6% Core lesson: outcome-tested harness engineering can outperform much larger prompted generalist models https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02276 https://github.com/DeepExperience/Harness-R1 https://x.com/alex_verem/status/2084986586496954648 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mYx3r8YA-HY Vibe-coding startup Lovable raises $400M at $13.3B valuation Lovable hit $500 Mln ARR in June Founders: Anton Osika and Fabian Hedin

slides.title: Mark Zuckerberg - AI Access vs Compute Mark
slides.text: Mark Zuckerberg - AI Access vs Compute Mark Zuckerberg - AI Access vs Compute https://about.fb.com/news/2026/08/the-future-is-for-everyone/ https://www.theverge.com/tech/977395/meta-mark-zuckerberg-superintelligent-ai-ramble https://www.facebook.com/zuck/posts/i-wrote-about-why-we-believe-the-future-is-for-everyone-more-coming-about-a-posi/10117806351954741/ https://www.facebook.com/FoxBusiness/videos/new-meta-founder-and-ceo-mark-zuckerberg-outlining-his-ai-vision-for-a-world-whe/1331806370010628/ Mark Zuckerberg advocates personal superintelligence: free or affordable AI, open models, individual agency, invention, entrepreneurship, tutoring, health support, and broad scientific progress He rejects safety through concentration of power, arguing that institutions alone cannot align AI with everyone’s values. The central critique is economic: model access is not equal capability when compute, energy, data centers, and capital remain finite Wealthier firms or litigants can buy more inference, parallel research, and stronger agents, preserving or amplifying existing advantages Broad access can improve defense, innovation, and long-tail problem solving, but fairness needs compute distribution - not merely open-weight models

slides.title: Double Descent Explained https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NP8oGdiu8dQ https://mlu-explain.github.io/double-descent/ https://github.com/josch14/double-descent https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.1903070116 https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.11118
slides.text: Double Descent Explained https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NP8oGdiu8dQ https://mlu-explain.github.io/double-descent/ https://github.com/josch14/double-descent https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.1903070116 https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.11118 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lJIW8TaAxLo Everyone learns the same rule: make a model too big and it overfits, memorizing the noise in the training data until it fails on everything new The classic bias-variance curve says test error is U-shaped, so you find the sweet spot and stop But modern neural networks have far more parameters than training examples , sit way past that sweet spot, and still generalize beautifully. How? The answer is a curve that seems to break the rule. As you keep adding parameters, test error climbs exactly as the textbook predicts, peaking at the interpolation threshold, the point where the model has just enough capacity to thread every training point and drive training error to zero Right there the fit is forced through every noisy point with no slack, so it swings wildly and generalizes worst. But push past the threshold and test error descends a second time, often below the classical sweet spot Once there are more parameters than points, infinitely many perfect fits exist, and gradient descent quietly prefers the smoothest, lowest-norm one More parameters give it more room to stay smooth, which is why a giant network that memorizes its training set can still be the one that generalizes best This is double descent , and it is why in deep learning, bigger really can be better.

slides.title: AI Updates AI Dev Platforms: GitHub vs Vercel
slides.text: AI Updates AI Dev Platforms: GitHub vs Vercel vs Replit AI has made software coding a cheap commodity The value of dev platform shifts from coding to orchestration, production, and verification GitHub - coordinates multi-vendor agents through familiar issues, pull requests, policies, and isolated task environments Vercel - focuses on safely converting generated code into production deployments using isolated microVM sandboxes and usage-aligned compute Replit - emphasizes autonomous verification. Its agent drives a browser, tests workflows, detects broken “Potemkin” interfaces, and attempts repairs MCP is the shared interoperability layer, enabling agents to access tools, data, and APIs through standardized servers The strategic tradeoff is clear: .. GitHub owns workflow governance .. Vercel owns deployment reliability .. Replit owns testing confidence https://blog.bytebytego.com/p/github-vs-vercel-vs-replit-what-dev https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8a4_AAds0vU

slides.title: granian vs uvicorn for SaaS Peter Diamandis -
slides.text: granian vs uvicorn for SaaS Peter Diamandis - Automagical Life https://www.diamandis.com https://metatrends.substack.com/p/auto-magical-living Diamandis predicts that by 2028, ambient AI will continuously use consented personal data to anticipate needs and act without explicit prompts It would combine calendars, conversations, home cameras, location, wearables, glucose data, and health records to optimize decisions and environments Examples include a robot chef tailoring meals, an autonomous car arriving at departure, and a living room adapting to stress Shopping agents could make approved purchases within budgets, while meeting assistants brief users, detect skepticism, draft follow-ups, and update CRM records The proposed exchange is pervasive surveillance for convenience, health support, and productivity; it also creates opportunities in permissions, privacy, robotics, health data, and logistics

slides.title: granian vs uvicorn for SaaS https://uvicorn.dev https://github.com/Kludex/uvicorn https://github.com/emmett-framework/granian
slides.text: granian vs uvicorn for SaaS https://uvicorn.dev https://github.com/Kludex/uvicorn https://github.com/emmett-framework/granian https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/deployment/manually/ https://talkpython.fm/books/python-in-production/chapter-6-running-on-rust Granian is a production HTTP application server for Python, written in Rust You run it in front of a Python web app (such as FastAPI) much as you would run Uvicorn or Gunicorn Granian supports ASGI, WSGI, HTTP/2, HTTPS, and WebSockets, making it compelling for connection-heavy or unusually high-throughput APIs Choose Granian when HTTP/ASGI layer is a bottleneck. Granian's Rust/Tokio implementation can improve throughput and tail latency. Choose Uvicorn first for most FastAPI SaaS deployments: it is mature, ubiquitous, well documented, and FastAPI’s default production server Database, Redis, external APIs, serialization, and Python CPU work usually dominate SaaS request time, limiting server-level gains. Uvicorn has the safer operational path: familiar tooling, broad ecosystem coverage, straightforward workers, and easier incident troubleshooting. # app.py from fastapi import FastAPI app = FastAPI() @app.get("/") async def index(): return {"status": "ok"} # run_server.py import subprocess import sys cmd = [ sys.executable, "-m", "granian", "--interface", "asgi", "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", "8000", "--workers", "2", "app:app", ] subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)

slides.title: AI Updates LangGraph: Runtime Over Diagrams https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/ https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph
slides.text: AI Updates LangGraph: Runtime Over Diagrams https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/ https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/overview https://www.blog.langchain.com/making-it-easier-to-build-human-in-the-loop-agents-with-interrupt/ https://www.youtube.com/@LangChain LangGraph’s core value is durable, stateful execution - not drawing agent flowcharts. State, nodes, edges, reducers, and compile define the graph ; supersteps coordinate parallel updates deterministically Checkpointers plus a thread ID preserve state, enable resume, human approval pauses, replay, forking, and streaming Use durable storage such as SQLite or Postgres; in-memory checkpoints disappear on restart Interrupts restart their enclosing node when resumed, so side effects must be retry-safe Prefer simpler loops for short, deterministic workflows without recovery or human-in-the-loop needs

slides.title: AI Updates AI Coding Skills: Modular Control https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8D8ewFBJfFM
slides.text: AI Updates AI Coding Skills: Modular Control https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8D8ewFBJfFM Matt Pocock’s modular AI-development skills aim to reduce unpredictable coding output by gathering precise project context. The approach favors short, reusable, independently runnable skills over rigid chained workflows. Groom Me interviews users one decision at a time, recommends options, and waits for confirmation before acting. Two Spec preserves the agreed design in a code-free specification, encouraging agents to inspect current code rather than copy stale snippets. Two Tickets slices work by end-to-end features rather than database/API/UI layers, enabling earlier testing. Implement emphasizes test-driven development; Code Review uses concise refactoring concepts such as shotgun surgery, feature envy, and data clumps.

slides.title: Karpathy’s Prompting 2.0 Karpathy’s Prompting 2.0 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eMPWBunaOic https://karpathy.ai
slides.text: Karpathy’s Prompting 2.0 Karpathy’s Prompting 2.0 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eMPWBunaOic https://karpathy.ai https://github.com/karpathy https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices https://x.com/karpathy/status/2079610838143623371 Andrej Karpathy’s “ramble session” prompting approach uses roughly 10 minutes of unstructured voice input to give an LLM richer project context. Start by warning the model that speech recognition may introduce typos, then freely describe goals, constraints, uncertainties, examples, preferences, and half-formed ideas. The model can reconstruct that messy context into a clearer shared understanding, sometimes through a short interview-style back-and-forth. Use it chiefly at the beginning of a new project or session, rather than for every small edit. The goal is fewer correction cycles and a stronger “mind meld,” not replacing clear acceptance criteria, tests, or verification Harness Influence Local AI Performance "OMP" stands for Oh My Pi , terminal-based AI coding agent OMP’s planning, iteration, and tool workflow improve outcomes but consume substantially more tokens and time https://omp.sh https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi https://hkinsley.com/reflections/right-harness-is-all-you-need https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H50xoAzNfB0 - sentdex

slides.title: AI Updates Claude Code Token Leak Fixes The
slides.text: AI Updates Claude Code Token Leak Fixes The video pitches four free tools to stretch Claude Code usage: RTK (Rust Token Killer) reduces shell output; https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk Caveman skill makes replies terse - https://caveman.so Ponytail discourages speculative code - https://ponytail.dev OmniRoute routes to 268 providers - https://omniroute.online Claimed results include 82.9% less tool-output usage, 69% fewer reply tokens, and roughly half the generated work volume The practical habits are sound: clear or compact stale context, trim CLAUDE.md, plan before executing, batch related requests, delegate exploration, and retain durable project memory. Be cautious with “free” routing: providers have quotas, privacy implications, changing availability, and potentially weaker models. Independent testing found more modest, variable savings for several tools; validate on representative repositories before standardizing https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman https://alexriosme.substack.com/p/there-is-a-reason-that-caveman-is https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute https://blog.jetbrains.com/ai/2026/07/ponytail-skill-claude-tested/ https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/how-reduce-claude-code-token-usage-rtk-omniroute-julian-goldie-phvwc https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_8GF2zIJf9w Normal: Authentication likely fails because the token expiry check uses local time. Caveman : Auth fails. Local-time expiry check. Use UTC. Add this sentence to agent rules file: Answer concisely. Be brief and to the point . Add a second sentence: Drop filler words, articles, and hedging when appropriate. Keep technical terms and code blocks exact.

slides.title: AI Updates Kestra: Governed AI Agents Kestra combines
slides.text: AI Updates Kestra: Governed AI Agents Kestra combines deterministic orchestration with AI reasoning , keeping high-impact actions under human control YAML workflows are versionable, reviewable, deployable through CI/CD, and recoverable through execution history, replays, and backfills A GitHub triage flow deterministically fetches issue facts, then lets an AI agent classify, prioritize, label, and draft a response. A pause or human-approval gate separates AI analysis from external writes; GitHub comments and labels are applied only after explicit approval. Kestra can self-host locally with Docker or Kubernetes, supports multiple scripting languages, and provides broad integrations for production automation https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra https://kestra.io https://kestra.io/blogs/introducing-ai-agents https://kestra.io/blogs/release-1-1 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7wnjIZ70MVk

slides.title: AI Updates Hermes /learn docs into skills Hermes
slides.text: AI Updates Hermes /learn docs into skills Hermes Agent’s /learn command can turn a PDF, book, or document collection into a reusable agent skill instead of treating it as temporary chat context The resulting skill can organize source material into focused, on-demand references, allowing the agent to retrieve relevant sections rather than repeatedly loading an entire document. This is useful for SOPs, architecture standards, brand guides, technical manuals, and frequently consulted books. Treat “permanent knowledge” cautiously: skills are local artifacts that should be reviewed, versioned, tested against source material, and updated when documents change. Start with one high-value, stable document your team repeatedly uses; validate answers with known questions before expanding the library https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/ https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent https://github.com/virgiliojr94/book-to-skill https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0sDKQMO23xE

slides.text: AI Updates Pax Silica: Philippine AI Bet Pax Silica is a US-led initiative for secure AI, semiconductor, minerals, energy, manufacturing, and logistics supply chains . The Philippines plans its first AI-native industrial hub at New Clark City, Tarlac: roughly 1,620 hectares (4,000 acres). It is proposed as industrial infrastructure, not a hyperscale data-center campus. Initial development covers about 500 hectares and is targeted within three to five years. Supporters expect investment, semiconductor upgrading, exports, and digital jobs. Critics demand enforceable safeguards for water, energy, land rights, transparency, and local benefits https://www.state.gov/pax-silica https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1281392 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sO-jLp8jSe4

slides.title: AI Updates Sybase & Microsoft SQL Server Sybase
slides.text: AI Updates Sybase & Microsoft SQL Server Sybase was founded in 1984, built an early high-performance client-server relational database, initially called Sybase SQL Server In 1988, Sybase, Microsoft, and Ashton-Tate jointly developed an OS/2 SQL Server; Microsoft initially marketed Sybase technology In 1993 they split. Microsoft paid Sybase for a licensed source-code base for its Windows direction; the products then evolved independently Sybase renamed its database as Adaptive Server Enterprise in the late 1990s to distinguish it from Microsoft SQL Server SAP acquired Sybase for about $5.8 Billion in 2010 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sybase https://www.sap.com/products/technology-platform/sql-server.html https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs https://community.sap.com/t5/additional-blog-posts-by-sap/a-deeper-look-at-sybase-history-of-ase/ba-p/12923660 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dK5iwBxFzGI SAP Sybase ASE and IQ are traditional transactional and analytics databases, not AI-native platforms For built-in AI features such as machine learning, embeddings, similarity search, forecasting, and anomaly detection, SAP’s primary platform is HANA Cloud.
